title: Python Logical Operators
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of python logical operators.
Choose the correct operators for common Python expressions.
Distinguish this operator family from related Python operators.
Apply the operators in a small, readable program.

understand.concept: The logical operators and, or and not combine or invert truth values. Python uses short-circuit evaluation: and stops when its left operand is false, while or stops when its left operand is true. These operators return one of their operands, not necessarily a bool, although they are commonly used with Boolean expressions.
understand.whyItMatters: Logical operators combine multiple conditions and can prevent unsafe or unnecessary evaluations.
understand.analogy: Logical conditions are like a checklist: AND requires every condition, OR requires at least one, and NOT reverses a truth value.
understand.analogyLimit: Because and and or return operands, expressions such as value or fallback may return a non-Boolean value. Truthiness is not the same as an explicit True or False object.

explain.narrative:
## 1. and

`A and B` needs both operands to be truthy. If A is false, Python does not evaluate B.

## 2. or

`A or B` needs at least one operand to be truthy. If A is true, Python skips B.

## 3. not

`not` reverses truthiness and returns a Boolean.

## 4. Short-circuit behavior

Short-circuiting can guard operations, such as checking that a list is not empty before reading its first item. Remember that `and` and `or` return an operand.

examples.title: Both conditions with and
examples.code:
age = 22
has_id = True
print(age >= 18 and has_id)
examples.explanation: Both operands are truthy, so the combined condition is true.

examples.title: Either condition with or
examples.code:
is_weekend = False
is_holiday = True
print(is_weekend or is_holiday)
examples.explanation: The or expression is true when at least one operand is truthy.

examples.title: Invert with not
examples.explanation: The not operator reverses the truth value.

examples.title: Guard an empty list
examples.explanation: The second condition is skipped when items is empty, avoiding an IndexError.

examples.title: Logical operators return operands
examples.explanation: The or operator returns the first truthy operand, or the last operand if none is truthy.

practise.guidedTask: Create three Boolean variables for age eligibility, membership and account status. Combine them with and, or and not.
practise.independentTask: Write a safe check that reads the first item only when a list is non-empty. Use a fallback label with or and explain its returned value.
hints: and requires both sides to be truthy.
or needs at least one truthy side.
The right side may be skipped.
Use short-circuiting to guard indexing or division.
practise.challenge: Predict which expressions evaluate their right-hand side. Demonstrate short-circuiting with a function that prints when it is called.

questions.prompt: When does A and B short-circuit?
questions.explanation: A false left operand determines the result of and.

questions.prompt: When does A or B skip B?
questions.explanation: A truthy left operand determines the result of or.
or returns the first truthy operand.

questions.prompt: Why is items and items[0] safe for an empty list?
options: The second operand is skipped when items is empty
and always converts lists to strings
questions.answer: The second operand is skipped when items is empty
questions.explanation: Short-circuit evaluation prevents the index expression from running.
